sanskrit:
यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते।
हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते।।
image_english: One not motivated by false ego, whose intelligence is not entangled, does not kill even if he kills.
caption:
Chapter 18, Verse 17

The freedom from killing. ‘yasya nāhaṅkṛto bhāvo’ (One who is not motivated by false ego). ‘buddhir yasya na lipyate’ (Whose intelligence is not entangled). ‘hatvāpi sa imāṁ l lokān’ (Though he kills men in this world). ‘na hanti na nibadhyate’ (He does not kill, nor is he bound by his actions). This applies to Arjuna. Since he is fighting as an instrument of Daivam (Kṛṣṇa’s will) without personal ego (‘Ahankara’), the act of killing is not ‘his’ act. He is like a soldier firing on the General’s order. The karma goes to the General (who can handle it), not the soldier.
